chapters.title: Chapter 1: Probability, Information Theory, and Evaluation Metrics
chapters.description: Foundations of uncertainty and information used to quantify model performance and to reason about segmentation and compression of sequences.
subtopics: Shannon entropy and conditional entropy
Cross-entropy and negative log-likelihood
KL divergence and model uncertainty
Perplexity and its interpretation
Bits-Per-Byte (BPB) as a tokenizer-independent metric
Estimating next-token/next-byte entropy
Relationship between entropy and compressibility

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Neural Language Modeling
chapters.description: Core concepts of language modeling, training objectives, autoregressive generation, and evaluation methods for sequence models.
subtopics: Autoregressive vs. auto-encoding models
Next-token prediction and teacher forcing
Maximum likelihood training and cross-entropy loss
Training and evaluation splits, overfitting considerations
Generation methods: greedy, sampling, beam search
Common benchmark tasks (classification, QA, code generation)

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Transformer: Architecture and Components
chapters.description: Detailed explanation of the Transformer building blocks used in modern LLMs.
subtopics: Scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention
Feed-forward networks (FFN) and activation functions (GELU, SwiGLU)
Residual connections and pre/post LayerNorm
Positional encodings: absolute, relative, RoPE (rotary embeddings)
Causal masking for autoregressive models
Parameterization choices and typical layer dimensions

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Efficient Attention Mechanisms and Implementations
chapters.description: Techniques and implementations to reduce attention compute and memory for long sequences and dynamic masks.
subtopics: Attention complexity and scalability (O(n^2) issues)
Windowed and local attention
Sparse and block-sparse attention patterns
FlashAttention: fused kernels and memory-efficient attention
FlexAttention and dynamic-mask fused implementations
Practical considerations for training large models

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Tokenization and Subword Methods
chapters.description: How text is converted into model input units, trade-offs of different tokenization schemes, and properties of tokenizers.
subtopics: UTF-8 encoding and byte-level representation
Word, subword, and byte-level vocabularies
Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) and SentencePiece
Vocabulary size trade-offs and embedding table implications
Tokenization sensitivity, biases, and multilingual issues
Incremental vs. non-incremental tokenization

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Byte- and Character-Level Modeling
chapters.description: Motivations, challenges, and prior approaches for modeling raw bytes or characters instead of tokenized units.
subtopics: Advantages of byte-level models (OOV handling, orthography)
Sequence length inflation and computational challenges
Prior byte/character models (CharRNNs, ByteNet, ByT5)
Strategies for reducing cost (downsampling, local models)
Evaluation nuances when comparing tokens vs bytes

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Hierarchical and Latent-Array Architectures
chapters.description: Architectures that operate at multiple scales (local bytes vs. global latents), and methods to map between them.
subtopics: Motivation for hierarchical processing (local vs global context)
Latent arrays and Perceiver-style latent representations
Pooling and readout operations from input to latents
Encoder-decoder splits and roles of local/global modules
Block-causal and hierarchical attention masks

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Cross-Attention Mechanisms
chapters.description: Detailed mechanics of cross-attention, its role in mapping between representations, and design patterns in encoder/decoder modules.
subtopics: Query-Key-Value roles in cross-attention
Cross-attention vs. self-attention: use cases and masks
Initializing queries (learned, pooled, hashed)
Multi-head cross-attention math and implementation
Residual and normalization patterns around cross-attention

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Segmentation and Patching Concepts
chapters.description: General approaches to grouping fine-grained input units into coarser processing steps and the implications for compute and modeling.
subtopics: Static (strided) patching and downsampling
Boundary-based patching heuristics (whitespace, delimiter rules)
Principles of adaptive segmentation (information-uniform windows)
Incremental segmentation constraints for generation
Trade-offs between patch size, context length, and compute

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Hashing, n-gram Features, and Sparse Embeddings
chapters.description: Techniques for representing local context with compact parameterizations using hashed features and n-grams.
subtopics: n-gram construction over bytes/characters
Rolling polynomial hashes (RollPolyHash) and implementation
Hash embedding tables and collision handling
Frequency-based vs hashed n-gram representations
Normalization and integration with learned embeddings

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Optimization, Regularization, and Training Schedules
chapters.description: Common optimization algorithms and hyperparameter schedules used when training large Transformer models.
subtopics: AdamW optimizer and typical hyperparameter choices
Learning rate warm-up, cosine decay, and schedules
Weight decay, gradient clipping, and stability tricks
Batch composition and batching on bytes vs tokens
Initialization practices and transfer learning considerations

chapters.title: Chapter 12: FLOPs, Compute Accounting, and Scaling Laws
chapters.description: How to estimate computational cost, reason about compute budgets, and apply scaling law principles to model/data trade-offs.
subtopics: Counting forward and backward FLOPs for Transformer layers
Contributions to FLOPs: attention, FFN, projections, output vocab
Inference vs training FLOP differences
Chinchilla-style compute-optimal parameter/data trade-offs
Interpreting and controlling compute in experiments

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Evaluation Protocols, Benchmarks, and Robustness Testing
chapters.description: Standard benchmarks, metrics, and strategies for assessing generalization, robustness, and downstream capabilities.
subtopics: Classification and reasoning benchmarks (MMLU, HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC)
Code generation evaluations (HumanEval, MBPP) and pass@k
Machine translation metrics (BLEU, SentencePiece BLEU, FLORES)
Character-level benchmarks and manipulation tasks (G2P, orthography tests)
Robustness tests: character-level noise strategies and analysis

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Software Primitives and Practical Implementations
chapters.description: Implementation-level knowledge and tools that enable efficient research and deployment of Transformer-based models.
subtopics: Frameworks: PyTorch ecosystem and best practices
Efficient kernels: FlashAttention, fused kernels and memory management
Dynamic masking and batching strategies for variable-length units
Packing and padding strategies to improve throughput
Profiling and measuring wall-clock time vs theoretical FLOPs
